projects.name: ACTIVATE Bangkok Project
projects.description: The ACTIVATE BANGKOK project, “Accelerating Climate-Resilient Transit-Oriented Inclusive and Vibrant Areas for Everyone in the Bangkok Metropolitan Area,” addresses urban mobility, climate resilience, and inclusivity in Bangkok. In promoting Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), the project integrates public transport, land use, and non-motorized transport (NMT) to reduce private vehicle dependence, enhance public transport accessibility, and promote inclusive development. Central to the approach of the project is the development and application of context-based TOD typologies to guide site selection and prioritise interventions, ensuring that climate resilience and accessibility improvements are embedded in all phases of the project.

projects.name: Address marine hypoxic zones by curbing coastal nutrient pollution from tourism, agriculture, and fishing ports and seafood processing in Thailand.
projects.description: The project will work at national level and aim to address marine hypoxic zones by curbing coastal nutrient pollution from tourism, agriculture, and fishing ports and seafood processing in Thailand. The project will address the above identified root causes and barriers by (i) improving existing monitoring systems, increase data sharing between stakeholder groups, and raising nutrient awareness among government agencies, NGOs and CSOs, farmers, and coastal communities; (ii) supporting policy coherence through interministerial sub-committee meetings and developing and implementing 6 nutrient pollution reduction strategies and action plans; (iii) testing and evaluating 7 pilots that address nutrient pollution in the agricultural, tourism and fishing port sectors, delivering capacity building programs on sustainable nutrient management practices; establishing a financing mechanisms for nutrient pollution management, and delivering sustainable nutrient investment training programs to private sector, investors and women entrepreneurs

projects.name: Advancing gender-responsive procurement in the Mekong subregion [WE RISE Together (2.0)]
projects.description:
WE RISE Together aims to facilitate more equal market opportunities for women entrepreneurs by advancing gender-responsive procurement in the Mekong subregion, and Thailand is a core implementation country for this work. In this phase, the project will systematically mainstream gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across implementation to ensure women-owned businesses and gender-responsive enterprises, including disabilities, rural entrepreneurs, ethnic minorities can participate and benefit more equitably from procurement opportunities. Building on collaborations and lessons from Phase 1 (2022–2025), and working through the existing management and coordination structure.

The project will consolidate and expand partnerships with both public and private sector actors to strengthen commitment and adopt the gender responsive procurement concepts into their policy and practices.

projects.name: Equitable access to quality, integrated and people-centred health services improved for women, children, migrants and vulnerable populations through strengthened primary health care, gender-responsive and safeguarding approaches, disease prevention, and continuity of care.
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates four former sub-outputs: "Maintaining the Triple elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) and optimized prevention cascades for key populations" (ID 207673); "Maternal and child health policies and quality of care improved" (ID 207694); "Prevention of sexual exploitation and gender equality capacity strengthened" (ID 207699); and "Migrant health strategy improved and the HINT data platform to include migrant populations expanded" (ID 207702). Leadership on the triple elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) was sustained through revitalization of the National Validation Committee, with interventions optimizing the prevention cascade, including maternal syphilis treatment at the primary health care level and strengthened comprehensive prevention programmes for young people. Maternal and child health policies were strengthened through successful advocacy for extending maternity leave to 120 days, high-level engagement on preterm birth management, leadership on breastfeeding in ASEAN and global forums, and strengthened hospital surveyor capacity for assessing youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services. Institutional capacity for gender equality and safeguarding was strengthened through advocacy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PRSEAH) with the Ministry of Public Health, alongside enhanced gender mainstreaming capacity among implementing partners. Access to health services for migrants was improved through advancement of the Migrant Health Strategy and expansion of the HINT data platform, supported by the Thailand Migration Report 2024 analyzing healthcare access for 5.3 million non-Thai residents, and strengthened operational capacity through field visits, training and human resource management.

projects.name: Enhance the protection of women migrant workers and migrant children by strengthening legal frameworks, improving prevention and protection mechanism and increasing access to essential services to prevent abuse, exploitation, harassment, violence, and trafficking. (PROTECT)
projects.description:
Joint Program PROTECT, implemented jointly by UNODC, ILO, UNICEF and UN Women. Under UN Women, the program was implemented in two countries: Cambodia and Thailand

Program objectives are (1) to strengthen national legislation, policies and regional frameworks for the protection of women migrant workers, children and other vulnerable groups in line with international standards; (2) to improve national and regional prevention and protection mechanisms to reduce rights’ violations against migrant women, children, and other vulnerable groups, including victims of trafficking and smuggled migrants; and (3) to increase the access of at-risk groups, women migrant workers and children to information, social and legal services, counselling, and association to prevent abuse, exploitation, harassment, violence, and trafficking in human beings.

projects.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Improving national capability to prepare, prevent, detect and respond to public health emergencies (PHE)" (ID 82366); "Regional health security and national risk assessment capacities strengthened" (ID 207683); "Emergency response operations and mass gathering preparedness supported" (ID 207684); "National health security capacities and IHR systems strengthened" (ID 207685); and "Risk communication and community-based emergency preparedness strengthened" (ID 207686). WHO supported the establishment of the Secretariat for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED) and strengthened national surveillance by integrating the Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment (QIRA) tool into the Standard Operating Procedures of National Situation Awareness Teams. Emergency response capacity was bolstered through procurement of essential supplies for the cholera response to spillover cases from Myanmar, the provision of shelter and psychosocial support materials for the border conflict response, and support to the Ministry of Public Health for mass gathering preparedness during the SEA Games. National preparedness was further enhanced through implementation of the Hospital Safety Index across Ministry of Public Health hospitals, strengthened provincial Emergency Operations Center capacities, upgraded Event-Based and genomic Surveillance for respiratory pathogens in high-tourism locations, and establishment of the National IHR Authority. Risk communication was advanced by piloting the Information Environment Assessment to address infodemics and by strengthening linkages between the Public Health Emergency Operations Center's risk communication channels and Village and Migrant Health Volunteer networks.

projects.name: Disease burden reduced through strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship, accelerated neglected tropical disease elimination efforts, and implementation of evidence-informed policies and multisectoral actions for noncommunicable disease prevention and control.
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates eight former sub-outputs: "Promoting evidence-based advocacy and implementing robust health and economic monitoring mechanisms for managing NCDs... (Strategies 3, 4 & 5)" (ID 82469); "Improve the quality and reach of essential health services" (ID 182895); "National workforce strategies strengthened and National Health Assembly resolution 2024 on transforming workforce for healthy society" (ID 207682); "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) surveillance and stewardship enhanced" (ID 207687); "Neglected Tropical Disease elimination and treatment supported" (ID 207690); "Mental health promotion, surveillance, and digital services expanded" (ID 207691); "Healthy ageing and integrated care for older people promoted" (ID 207696); and "NCD risk factor reduction policies and enforcement mechanisms strengthened" (ID 207697). Multisectoral action on NCDs was enhanced through improved partnerships facilitated by the UN Thematic Working Group, aligned with NCD Strategies 3, 4 and 5, complementing the workforce strengthening achieved through enhanced HRH provider registries and a landscape analysis of the community non-professional workforce. Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) management was advanced through co-hosting a Multi-Country Meeting on AMR and Primary Health Care, a Point Prevalence Survey on healthcare-associated infections across 100 hospitals, and development of a national AMR burden methodology and antimicrobial stewardship tools. Progress towards elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases was supported through provision of diagnostic test strips for Lymphatic Filariasis and sustained treatment of leprosy cases through procurement and distribution of essential medication. Mental health services were expanded through the nationwide scale-up of the "Step-by-Step" digital application, the "Tor term Jai" platform, and the WHO LIVE LIFE suicide prevention package, alongside capacity building through the 3rd International Mental Health Workforce Training. Healthy ageing was promoted through implementation of the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach with Siriraj Hospital, alongside advocacy to address social isolation among older persons. NCD risk factor reduction was advanced through sustained advocacy for "Best Buys" policies, including health taxes, e-cigarette bans, food reformulation, Milk Code enforcement, and alcohol control policy assessment.
projects.outcome: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.

projects.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Facilitate and enhance integrated care for older people through the use of mobile health technology" (ID 82412); "Progressive development of legislation on control of marketing of food and non-alcoholic beverage for children" (ID 82467); "Health policies and collective action against NCDs... (Strategies 1 and 2)" (ID 82468); "Evidence-based parenting and violence prevention programs scaled up" (ID 207692); and "Urban governance for Healthy Cities strengthened" (ID 207695). Integrated care for older people was advanced through mobile health technology, complementing broader NCD policy work that promoted increased investment in NCDs through targeted communication strategies based on Thailand's scale-up findings, aligned with NCD Strategies 1 and 2. Legislative development on marketing controls for food and non-alcoholic beverages targeting children was progressed through technical support and policy advocacy, contributing to the wider NCD risk-reduction agenda. Child protection and development were fostered through the scale-up of evidence-based parenting programmes and high-level advocacy, complemented by the 2nd global survey on Violence Against Children to generate data for policy formulation. Urban health governance was strengthened through capacity building for local authorities, with the Healthy Cities approach recognized through awards to four Thai cities for their commitment to health-promoting urban environments.

projects.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "Conducted a national landscape assessment and developed an implementation plan to reduce dental amalgam use and mercury waste emissions" (ID 207704) and "Pioneered community-based air pollution interventions, including 'clean air shelters' and alternative crop promotion" (ID 207705). WHO collaborated with Thailand's Department of Health to implement the WHO-UNEP Global Environment Facility (GEF) project, accelerating national implementation of the Minamata Convention's dental amalgam provisions through a comprehensive assessment of policies, regulatory frameworks and waste management practices. In parallel, WHO supported the Government in promoting community-based air pollution interventions in high-risk regions, including Bangkok and Chiang Rai, where respiratory diseases linked to air quality are a major public health concern. projects.name: Thailand’s role in shaping key global health agendas and advancing sustainable health development strengthened through enhanced leadership, knowledge sharing, evidence-informed decision-making, and international collaboration, while supporting implementation of national health priorities and Country Cooperation Strategy outcomes.
projects.description: This sub-output is carried forward from the former sub-output: "Promoting the demonstrated collective leadership and contributions of Thailand in global health" (ID 90382), under the CCS EnLIGHT priority area of the 2022-2026 Country Cooperation Strategy. It enhances Team Thailand's collective capacity for international engagement in global health governance, focusing on two core functions: advancing key global health agendas and supporting other Country Cooperation Strategy programmes and partner agencies. This is achieved through four strategic actions: evidence generation, capacity development, international engagement, and knowledge management, including the establishment of resource centres and platforms and effective policy communication to support policy decisions.

projects.name: Improved equitable access to quality essential health services through strengthened immunization and disease surveillance systems, and implementation of evidence-based strategies for communicable and noncommunicable disease prevention, control and elimination.
projects.description: This sub-output consolidates four former sub-outputs: "National Tuberculosis control strategy and data usage improved" (ID 207688); "Malaria elimination strategies for Vivax malaria implemented" (ID 207689); "NCD management practices and monitoring frameworks improved by documenting best practices in the Diabetes Remission Initiative" (ID 207698); and "Immunization coverage and vaccine-preventable disease surveillance enhanced" (ID 207703). Tuberculosis control was advanced through the 1st National TB Conference, a comprehensive review of Thailand's TB epidemiological data, and piloting of AI-powered computer-aided detection for TB and early cancer detection in resource-limited settings. Malaria elimination efforts targeting Vivax malaria were advanced through the funding and introduction of a 7-day Primaquine and Tafenoquine treatment protocol, complemented by novel G-6PD deficiency testing to ensure safe treatment administration. NCD management and monitoring were strengthened by documenting best practices under the Diabetes Remission Initiative, developing a draft health-economics Monitoring and Evaluation framework, and implementing the WHO SEAHEARTS technical package in Lampang and Chiang Mai to improve hypertension management in primary health care. Immunization coverage was enhanced through the Vaccine Avengers Programme, which boosted measles-rubella coverage in low-performing provinces, alongside strengthened community outreach, real-time tracking dashboards, Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) surveillance, and continued support for Measles and Rubella elimination and Polio-free status by 2026.

children.name: Human capital needed for social and inclusive development is improved through strengthening of institutions, partnerships and the empowerment of people.
children.description:
The second strategic outcome for consideration contributes to the NESDP priorities enhancing Thailand’s human capital. The underlying premise is that people represent the true wealth of the nation. A healthy, well-educated and skilled population, evidenced through the high human development index and based on the foundation of being able to access and exercise human rights, is a good in itself. It will act as a catalyst that drives the transformation of Thailand. The enabling environment for such a transformation is also dependent on the ability of public institutions, systems and services to successfully frame and implement a coherent integrated policy framework, based on principles of equity, accountability, transparency and efficiency. To affect such a change and achieve the impact required, public services need to concentrate on measures that drive standards and outcomes upwards through a focus on quality improvement. To focus the UN’s support on the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the Government and development partners including civil society, businesses and communities to prioritize two focus areas, which contribute to nine of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th Plan. 
- Human capital development through enhancing access to quality of public services,
- Digital inclusion and transformation

children.name: People living in Thailand, especially those at risk of being left furthest behind, are able to participate in and benefit from development, free from all forms of discrimination.
children.description: The aspiration to leave no one behind is the touchstone of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Women and LGBTI people in particular lag behind their male counterparts across much of Thailand’s social, economic and political life. The energy and dynamism of young people will play a key role in catalysing Thailand’s enterprising culture in the post-COVID-19 landscape. Equally, older people should experience healthy and active aging, as Thailand is an ageing society. Ethnic populations and people living in rural and remote areas should have equal opportunity to those residing in urban areas. Evidence consistently shows the criminalization, stigma, discrimination and other human rights violations towards people infected and affected by HIV reduce service uptake and increase HIV infection. As already noted, the digital divide, nationality as well as status can hold populations back from benefitting and contributing towards Thailand’s collective development journey. In short, where barriers to inclusion and development exist, they need to be systematically dismantled and replaced with enabling opportunities and services.
